summary: The basic flow is right: tap to select opens the docked sheet, the centre playhead is fixed, the trim/split row reads left to right as trim start, split, trim end, the edge grips need a 300ms hold and turn teal, and a clip moves after a still hold. But several claims fail for a real phone user. The three cut buttons only exist while the playhead is inside the clip; outside it, and right after a split, they are swapped for Move/Extend buttons. Their names ('Split at playhead' etc.) are tooltip titles that never show on a phone. Step 7 and the computer's 'drag the middle' run into the ⇄ Slip pill on any trimmed video clip, which slides the footage instead of moving the clip. On a computer, S extends the clip rather than splitting it when the playhead is off the clip. The troubleshooting line's 'let go too early' and 'until it lifts' are wrong: there is no lift visual, only a vibration that iPhones don't produce. All of this can be fixed by rewording.

missing: Most phone users edit a clip that fills the whole frame. For that clip the Drop Shadow tile is marked "does nothing here", the shadow can't be seen, Shadow only turns the screen black, and Glow past the edges changes nothing. The "make the clip smaller in Position / Scale" step needs to come before Drop Shadow is added, not in a closing note. summary: The flow is right and the labels match the code exactly: Effects card → + Add Effect → search → pick two (numbered) → "Add 2 effects" → open rows → Off/On buttons. It needs wording fixes, not a redo. Step 7 says "drag up", but the control is a horizontal ruler you drag left, and a vertical drag scrolls. Step 4 doesn't say to clear the old search text. Step 9's "raise Softness first" suggests Spread is locked, but Softness starts at 6 px, and Spread is only greyed out at Softness 0. Steps 8 and 10 promise results that only show when the clip doesn't fill the screen; on a full-screen clip Shadow only turns the screen black. So the "make it smaller" note has to move before step 4. The "On a computer" line is accurate, since the PC has used the same pick-then-Add flow since queue 303.
